neighbours.label: ' of' after ' shades' or ' tones', in colour and non-colour uses ('shades of grey', 'tones of concern', 'shades of meaning'); ' of' after other plural nouns stays low.
fire: The sea went through many shades of green.
Her report had subtle shades of meaning.
He spoke in hushed tones of concern.
The walls come in soft tones of cream.
Critics found several shades of irony in it.
The dress is sold in six shades of pink.
We heard rising tones of anger in the hall.
Old paper takes on warm tones of brown.
quiet: The sea went through many days of storm.
Her report had several pages of notes.
He spoke in long bursts of French.
The walls come in thin sheets of tin.
Critics found several lines of verse in it.
The dress is sold in six sizes of cotton.
We heard rising sounds of music in the hall.
Old paper takes on small spots of mold.
